message.reasoning:
I need to write JUnit 4 tests covering Token's package-private structure, including the static reset method, the Doctype subclass fields and getters, and the Tag subclass's reset and attribute-related behavior. The Tag logic I need to test includes newAttribute's handling of pending attribute names and values (trimming, empty checks, null cases), finaliseTag's attribute finalization, name validation that throws on null/empty, and the various appendTagName/appendAttributeName/appendAttributeValue methods that either initialize or concatenate string builders. Then I'm mapping out the remaining node types I need to test: StartTag with its attributes-aware toString, EndTag, Comment, Character, CData with its wrapped output format, and EOF. I'm sketching out the type-checking helper methods (isDoctype/asDoctype pairs for each node type) and the tokenType method, then planning a batch of test cases covering reset behavior, doctype getters, and various edge cases in attribute handling like empty names after trimming and pending attribute values. Continuing to lay out test cases covering tag finalization, name validation, and the attribute/tag name appending logic with its different builder states. - testIsCData - testTokenType Now I need to check jsoup's Validate.isFalse method, since this is part of the Jsoup-92b defect code—I should confirm whether it throws IllegalArgumentException when the condition is true. I'll write the test in the org.jsoup.parser package so it can access package-private classes, and I need to verify how Attributes.get(String key) behaves for checking stored values. I recall that jsoup's Attributes.get() returns an empty string if the key isn't found, but could return null if the value was explicitly set to null, so I should assert against attributes.get("name") cautiously given this ambiguity, noting it depends on the exact implementation behavior. Instead I'll lean on size() checks to verify whether an attribute was actually added, since that avoids depending on get()'s value quirks while still confirming each branch. I'll plan test cases checking that a null pendingAttributeName skips adding the attribute, then move on to covering the whitespace-only name case. I'm not fully certain how jsoup handles boolean attributes internally, so to stay safe I'll keep the test focused on Token's branches rather than Attributes internals—just verifying attributes.size() reflects whether newAttribute() added an entry or not, and only asserting specific stored values for the unambiguous cases like hasEmptyAttributeValue. So I'll test that a null-valued attribute's get() returns null, flagging this as an assumption from the jsoup source. For attributes not added due to invalid names, I'll just check size() stays unchanged, and since Tag itself is abstract, I'll instantiate a concrete EndTag to exercise its methods. I'll use EndTag specifically because its attributes field starts null, letting me test the lazy-initialization branch in newAttribute(). For appendAttributeValue with an int array, I'll cover both the empty-array no-op case and a populated array with actual codepoints. I also plan to directly test the package-private reset(StringBuilder) method, verify tokenType() on a Doctype instance returns the right simple name, and confirm that calling name() on an inappropriate token type triggers the expected Validate.isFalse exception. For CData, I'm checking that its constructor properly stores the data and that toString renders it wrapped in CDATA markers, including the edge case where null data gets stringified as "null". I'm also planning tests for EOF's reset behavior, confirming its type remains unchanged, and setting up is/as type-check tests for each token subtype to verify correct casting and false negatives across types. Then I move on to drafting the full test file, double-checking package placement and verifying the method signatures across all the Token subclasses before writing everything out. Since Tag is nested inside Token, it retains access to Token's private constructor even though it's private, so the implicit super() call compiles fine—but this means test code outside Token still can't directly instantiate Tag since it's abstract anyway. Now I'm planning assertions for appendAttributeValue with an int array of codepoints, expecting the resulting attribute value to concatenate into "abc", while noting this path also sets hasPendingAttributeValue and transfers any existing pending string value into the builder. For the empty int array case, I'm tracing through: since nothing gets appended, the builder stays empty, so newAttribute() falls back to checking pendingAttributeValueS, which would be null since that field was never populated along this path. Now I'm tracing the two-String-calls scenario: the first call sets pendingAttributeValueS directly since the builder is empty, but the second call triggers the builder to absorb that stored string before appending the new one, clearing pendingAttributeValueS back to null. Checking newAttribute() afterward confirms it reads from the builder when it's non-empty, giving "abcd" as expected, while a single call just reads pendingAttributeValueS directly without touching the builder. Next I'm verifying appendAttributeValue(char) always appends straight to the builder, bypassing the S field entirely. Now I want to test appendAttributeValue(char[]) the same way, then move on to verifying appendTagName and appendAttributeName on StartTag/EndTag, and confirm Tag.getAttributes() returns the same underlying attributes reference. For toString testing, I'll build a StartTag with a "div" name and an attribute, checking the output starts with "
" without asserting the exact attribute serialization format since that depends on Attributes.toString(). For a tag with no attributes, like "br", I expect toString() to return exactly "
" since the attributes object is empty by default. For EndTag, since attributes aren't initialized (null from Tag), calling name("p") should produce "

" in toString(). Now I'm moving to reset() tests: for Doctype, I'll set fields then call reset() and verify everything returns to defaults—empty name, null pubSysKey, empty identifiers, forceQuirks false. For StartTag reset, I need to verify attributes becomes a fresh empty Attributes object (not null) and tagName resets to null, accessing the protected tagName field directly since the test class shares the package. For Comment, I can directly mutate the package-private data StringBuilder and bogus flag, then confirm reset() clears both. For Character, since data is private, I'll rely on the public data()/getData() methods instead of direct field access. For EOF, reset() should return the same instance with type unchanged, which I'll verify with assertSame and checking TokenType.EOF. Next I want to test tokenType() returns the correct simple class name for each token type, then cover the isXxx/asXxx methods by creating one instance of each type and confirming correct type checks pass while others fail, including checking that casting to the wrong type throws ClassCastException. I'll also check isCData returns false for a non-CData Character instance. Now I'm verifying the Attributes API - checking that size(), get(String key), and put(String key, String value) are all public since Token in a different package calls attributes.put() directly when adding new attributes. I'm also confirming the Attributes() constructor is public, accessible for creating new attribute sets in StartTag, so tests can use it similarly. Now I need to recall Validate.isFalse's behavior to finish writing out the full test file. This confirms that a null or empty tag name triggers an IllegalArgumentException, matching my earlier assumption. Now I'm finalizing the list of test methods I plan to include: checking static StringBuilder reset behavior (both null-safe and clearing cases), verifying Doctype's default state, confirming reset restores defaults, and testing the Doctype getters. Continuing the test plan, I'm listing out additional cases covering the newAttribute logic for Tag -- handling missing pending names, whitespace-only names after trimming, lazy creation of the attributes map, empty and null value branches, single versus multi-append value building, appending char, char array, and int array values (both empty and non-empty), and finally confirming that finaliseTag properly adds any pending attribute. I'm continuing with tests for finaliseTag with no pending attribute, name validation throwing on null or empty input, normal name handling, appending tag and attribute names from null starts with concatenation, appending single characters, the empty attribute value flag, default self-closing state, and resetting the tag. Then I move into StartTag-specific tests covering constructor initialization, reset behavior, name/attribute combos, and toString with and without attributes, followed by EndTag's toString and default null attributes, and wrapping up with Comment's default state and reset behavior. Rounding out the list, I'm adding tests for Comment's toString, CharacterData's reset and toString, CData's toString and its isCharacter/isCData flags, EOF's reset preserving type, token type name mapping, and the full set of "is" checks across Doctype, StartTag, EndTag, Comment, Character, and EOF, plus confirming CData is false for a plain Character. This feels like solid coverage, so I'll trim a few overlapping cases for brevity and move on to writing the actual test file, making sure the imports are correct for JUnit and jsoup's node classes. Since Token and its nested static classes are package-private and TokenTest lives in the same package, I don't need to import Token itself to reference things like Token.Doctype or Token.StartTag.
